body: If the input is empty then '0' / NULL will be saved. CakePHP will not try and handle figuring out the default value for a column when saving.

@markstory Should it not transform the empty string into the valid default value? It has the schema available, thus it would be quite easy to avoid this fatal error by looking if "DEFAULT NULL" is set. If it is "DEFAULT NOT NULL" it should not automatically default to `null` here IMO.
It could, that might be difficult to do though.

Currently I also work around this issue in a few apps. Either as beforeSave() cast or something similar.
But I also see it as a deficiency in the current implementation.

If the default value for a column is "1" and the given value is empty, 
we will get opposite results. Currently, "0" will be saved.
It might be nice that we could define a validation rule such as 'allowEmpty' => 'default'.

@chinpei215 Having non-nullish default values is something I never did before. For this and other reasons :)
But I can understand that this behavior feels a little bit awkward.

@dereuromark  I use "NOT NULL DEFAULT 1" sometimes. such as field "is_active".
But it might be not fit in cake.
I think reading the available schema is a good way too :)

EDIT:
But it might break BC. That is the case I mentioned in my first comment.

@dereuromark Type probably, like Marks comment too ,-)

Anyway, I would prefer that solution too. Just cast it to _a_ default value instead of NULL if the field is defined NOT NULL. 0 would be my best guess too, but if a different DEFAULT is defined this could get really awkward, taking the (optional) DEFAULT definition into account would be a real winner!
